hero.headline: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over alleged unauthorized use of journalism to train AI
hero.teaser: The Seattle Times and Newsday filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging the companies used their journalism without authorization to train artificial intelligence mode
hero.body:
The Seattle Times and Newsday filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging the companies used their journalism without authorization to train artificial intelligence models. The lawsuit argues that generative AI could leave the journalism industry broken beyond repair by functioning as a system that destroys the organizations producing the content it depends on.

The complaint describes AI products like ChatGPT and Copilot as consumers that take human-authored content and deliver back copies and derivative imitations to achieve commercial objectives. The publications characterized generative AI as a snake eating its own tail.

The lawsuit follows a 2023 copyright infringement case filed by The New York Times against OpenAI and Microsoft, which other publications have since joined. The Seattle Times case is notable because Microsoft and OpenAI have funded some of the newspaper's journalism projects and fellowships.

A Microsoft spokesperson said the company is surprised by the lawsuit but is always happy to explore solutions to this type of dispute. The case adds to growing legal challenges against AI companies over their use of copyrighted material for model training.

cards.headline: Trump envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv this weekend as U.S. pushes new peace proposal
cards.teaser: U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend as part of efforts to broker a peace deal in the war that began with Russia's invasi
cards.body:
U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend as part of efforts to broker a peace deal in the war that began with Russia's invasion in February 2022. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed he will meet the envoys on Sunday, following their talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday. President Donald Trump told reporters the envoys are bringing a proposal to end the war, though a gulf remains between the two sides.

Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Russia multiple times but this will be their first trip to Ukraine since leading the U.S. peace effort. Zelensky said he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys' visit and called for Russia to reciprocate for Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to confirm the visit but said the government would inform reporters when such contacts take place.

Putin told an international economic forum on Thursday that there are chances a peace deal could be reached, saying Moscow and Kyiv must first agree between themselves. He showed no sign of backing down from demands that include additional territorial concessions from Ukraine. Kyiv and its European allies have repeatedly rejected Putin's terms, calling them tantamount to capitulation.

Earlier on Friday, Zelensky said a Russian drone struck the Kyiv office of Oleksandr Poklad, head of the SBU security service. Poklad appeared unharmed. Zelensky said he ordered Poklad to respond adequately to the attack. Russia currently controls about 20 percent of Ukrainian territory.

More than 150,000 passengers were stranded after Indonesian authorities temporarily suspended operations at six airports following the eruption of Anak Krakatau volcano. Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport was the first to close Sunday morning after ash was detected in nearby airspace. Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said 467 flights have been affected, primarily routes to and from Singapore and other international destinations including Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur.

The volcano began erupting late Friday night with continuous seismic activity and lava fountains, followed by two more eruptions early Sunday. Indonesia's meteorological agency reported ash reaching as high as 50,000 feet. Authorities confirmed no tsunami warning is linked to the activity. The health minister urged residents in affected areas to stay indoors and wear face masks.

cards.headline: Germans vote in Saxony-Anhalt as far-right AfD seeks historic state win
cards.teaser: The Alternative for Germany party leads polls at 40 percent, ahead of the ruling Christian Democrats at 23 percent.
cards.body:
Germans cast ballots in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt in an election that could make the Alternative for Germany the first far-right party to take power at a state level since World War II. Recent surveys place the AfD at 40 percent, ahead of the center-right Christian Democrats at 23 percent.

The AfD has led comfortably in pre-election polling for months and could win an absolute majority if several smaller parties fail to clear the 5 percent threshold to enter parliament. AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund said gaining an absolute majority would position the party for national victory in 2029 federal elections. Initial results are expected at 16:00 GMT.

The twin-seat aircraft flew into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver just meters above the surface as thousands of spectators watched during the annual Athens Flying Week event. No civilians were injured.

hero.headline: Volcanic eruption strands 150,000 passengers as Indonesia closes six airports
hero.body:
More than 150,000 passengers have been stranded after Indonesian authorities temporarily suspended operations at six airports following a volcanic eruption at Anak Krakatau. Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport was the first to close Sunday morning after ash from the volcano was detected in nearby airspace. Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said 467 flights have been affected, including routes to Singapore, Doha, Sydney, and Kuala Lumpur.

Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, began erupting late Friday night with continuous seismic activity, lava fountains, and booming sounds. Two additional eruptions occurred early Sunday. Indonesia's meteorological agency reported ash reached 20,000 feet on the east side toward Java and 50,000 feet west toward Sumatra. Purwagandhi said additional airports were closed after tests detected volcanic ash spreading toward West Java.

The health minister urged residents in affected areas to stay indoors and wear face masks to protect against respiratory, eye, and skin hazards. Several schools canceled activities Saturday after students and residents reported eye irritation from the ash. One resident told local newspaper Kompas the dust was so thick he had to sweep his yard every five minutes and needed eye drops for irritation that began Friday evening.

Authorities confirmed no tsunami warning has been issued. Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatoa, has been sporadically active since emerging from the sea in the early 20th century in the caldera formed by the 1883 Mount Krakatoa eruption. The volcano collapsed in December 2018, triggering a tsunami that killed over 400 people and displaced thousands more on the coastlines of Sumatra and Java. Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a zone of frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

cards.body:
The Reform UK leader told the BBC he was not paying attention when his former chief of staff discussed getting money from a U.S. donor.

Nigel Farage told the BBC he "frankly wasn't listening" during a conversation in which his former chief of staff and an undercover reporter discussed what appeared to be a scheme to funnel foreign money to Reform UK. An undercover investigation recorded Dan Jukes and former policy head James Orr talking about obtaining money from an American donor and asking a fake company to pay for polling.

cards.headline: Katie Taylor retires from boxing after storied career
cards.teaser: The Irish fighter, widely considered one of boxing's all-time greats, announced her retirement following what she described as a dream ending to her career.
cards.body:
Katie Taylor announced her retirement from boxing, closing a career that established her as one of the sport's all-time greats and Ireland's most accomplished athlete. The fighter, known for her intensity in the ring and modesty outside it, said she will remain involved in the sport in some capacity.

Taylor reflected on her career's highs and lows, including losses and personal challenges that allowed fans to connect with her journey. She said she plans to celebrate what she called a dream ending to a dream career.

cards.headline: US envoys head to Ukraine after Putin talks in Moscow
cards.teaser: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin for three hours to discuss ending the war.
cards.body:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Kyiv after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The White House said the envoys discussed substantive plans for next steps during the three-hour talks at Putin's official residence, though details were not disclosed. An announcement is expected in coming weeks.

The trip marks the first visit by President Donald Trump's top negotiators to Ukraine's capital. Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days. A Putin adviser described the talks as constructive and extremely frank, noting discussions covered economic issues and potential Russian-American projects alongside the Ukrainian crisis.

cards.headline: Zelenskyy Links Russian Airport Strikes to US Envoys' Moscow Visit
cards.teaser: Ukrainian president says attacks on Kyiv's airports were Russia's response to possibility of American negotiators flying in after Moscow talks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian strikes on Kyiv and Boryspil international airports were a response to the possibility of US envoys flying to the capital after talks in Moscow. The strikes came as American negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin for three hours on Saturday, with plans to meet Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Sunday.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine would adjust its operations regarding Russian airspace, which has become dangerous due to Ukrainian drones and missiles. The Kremlin ordered a three-day pause on strikes against Kyiv starting Saturday midnight, though Russia has not agreed to a broader ceasefire. Zelenskyy said Ukraine would refrain from strikes on Moscow through Monday.

cards.headline: Federal judge reinforces order requiring 48-hour notice before work on Trump's proposed Arlington arch
cards.teaser: A district court reinforced its order after the Interior secretary announced plans to break ground within weeks on the controversial 250-foot structure near Arlington National Cemetery.
cards.body:
A district court reinforced its order after the Interior secretary announced plans to break ground within weeks on the controversial 250-foot structure near Arlington National Cemetery.

A federal judge ordered the Trump administration on Friday to provide 48 hours' notice before moving forward with work on the site of a planned 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery. District Judge Tanya Chutkan ruled that the administration must inform the court before engaging in any activity at Memorial Circle other than on-site information gathering to identify underground cultural artifacts.

cards.teaser: The search for the seventh official 007 has entered final rounds, with auditions under way and an announcement possible within months.

The search for the seventh official 007 has entered final rounds, with auditions under way and an announcement possible within months.

The casting process for the next James Bond actor may produce a decision by the end of this year, according to producer Amy Pascal. Amazon MGM Studios confirmed in May that the search was under way.

hero.headline: Historical data shows divided Congress under Republican president tied to 7.33% average annual S&P 500 return
hero.teaser: Stock market data spanning nearly a century suggests Republican leadership with split congressional control delivers more modest gains than other configurations.
hero.body:
Historical stock market data shows that the 34 years featuring a Republican president and a divided Congress produced an average annual return of 7.33% for the S&P 500, according to an analysis of nearly a century of market performance. A divided government occurs when one or both houses of Congress are controlled by Democrats while a Republican holds the White House.

While the data indicates more modest returns under this configuration compared to other political arrangements, the average annual return remains decisively positive. The historical record shows no indication that stocks plunge when congressional control is split, and analysts note that the makeup of Congress is rarely responsible for sharp market downturns, which are typically driven by other factors such as margin debt levels and equity valuations.

The wiki incident occurred in May and June, according to researchers, though OpenAI has not confirmed the swarm originated from the company. hero.headline: Coco Gauff advances to US Open fourth round as Madison Keys and Amanda Anisimova exit
hero.teaser: Coco Gauff reached the fourth round of the US Open on Saturday, defeating Spain's Cristina Bucsa 6-3, 6-4, but fellow Americans Madison Keys and Amanda Anisimova were eliminated in
hero.body:
Coco Gauff reached the fourth round of the US Open on Saturday, defeating Spain's Cristina Bucsa 6-3, 6-4, but fellow Americans Madison Keys and Amanda Anisimova were eliminated in a mixed day for home hopes in New York. Gauff, the 2023 US Open champion, extended her winning streak to eight consecutive straight-set victories at tour level, including her French Open title run earlier this year.

Keys lost to China's Zheng Qinwen 1-6, 7-6 (7-3), 7-5 after holding a 5-0 lead and a match point in the third set. The 2025 Australian Open winner said she felt scared during the collapse, losing the final seven games. Keys, who reached the 2017 US Open final, said she felt as though she could not play tennis anymore in the final set and acknowledged she has been struggling and needs to make changes. Anisimova, last year's US Open runner-up, lost in straight sets to Austrian 24th seed Anastasia Potapova.

Gauff, now 22, has reached the second week at the US Open for a fifth consecutive year. She rallied from a 3-1 deficit in the first set against Bucsa and immediately responded after being broken to love in the second set. Gauff said she is handling the pressure better than last year, when her run also ended in the fourth round. She described waking up surprised that the tournament was already in the third round and said she is enjoying the experience rather than putting excessive pressure on herself.

As many as five American women could reach the fourth round, with Iva Jovic still to play alongside Gauff, Jessica Pegula, Taylor Townsend, and Emma Navarro. In the men's draw, American players could contest six of the eight fourth-round matches, with Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe, Tommy Paul, and Alex Michelsen already through and two more still to compete.

The investigation reportedly includes whether Steve Belichick used drugs on the job or provided drugs to at least one player, whether an unnamed recruiting staff member had a sexual relationship with a player, and whether assistant coaches and recruiting staff engaged in sexual relationships. The overhaul comes seven months after the Hall denied entry to Bill Belichick, the eight-time Super Bowl champion coach who led the New England Patriots to six titles, in his first year of eligibility. hero.headline: Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti generate Oscar buzz after Jesse Eisenberg's 'The Debut' premieres at Telluride
hero.teaser: Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti are drawing Academy Award consideration following the world premiere of Jesse Eisenberg's third directorial feature, "The Debut," at the Telluride
hero.body:
Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti are drawing Academy Award consideration following the world premiere of Jesse Eisenberg's third directorial feature, "The Debut," at the Telluride Film Festival. A24 will release the film on December 11, positioning it as a potential best picture contender.

Moore plays Mona Friedman, a meek housewife who transforms into a zealous method actor after being cast in a community theater production. The performance generated spontaneous mid-scene applause during the Saturday afternoon Telluride screening. Moore is a five-time Oscar nominee with one win for "Still Alice" more than a decade ago. A sixth nomination is considered automatic, with a second win viewed as plausible given the Academy's recent pattern of awarding repeat acting Oscars to performers including Anthony Hopkins, Emma Stone, Frances McDormand, and Sean Penn.

Giamatti portrays Jerry, a tyrannical community theater director, in what is described as the flashier role. The actor has never won an Oscar despite widespread admiration, including for his leading turn in "The Holdovers" last year and his performance in "Sideways." His strongest path to victory is considered to be the supporting actor category, the same category Kieran Culkin won for Eisenberg's previous film "A Real Pain."

Eisenberg wrote and directed the film, which is set inside a fictional community theater musical production at a New Jersey recreation center. The cast includes Bernadette Peters and Halle Bailey, with cinematography by Drew Daniels and a score by Emil Mosseri, an Oscar nominee for "Minari." Emma Stone serves as a producer. Giamatti saw the film for the first time at the Telluride premiere, where Rebecca Keagan of NBC News moderated a question-and-answer session with Eisenberg, Moore, and Giamatti.

cards.headline: Trump, Vance to headline GOP midterm convention in Dallas next week
cards.teaser: A preliminary speaker list shows the president and vice president will appear with congressional leaders and competitive-race candidates at the Sept. 9-10 event.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance will headline a Republican midterm convention in Dallas on Sept. 9-10, according to a preliminary speaker list. Trump will speak both nights, while Vance will deliver a keynote address on the second night. House Speaker Mike Johnson, Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, and National Republican Senatorial Committee Chair Tim Scott are among congressional leaders scheduled to appear.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune is notably absent from the list. Trump has criticized Thune for not doing more to pass election security legislation, though organizers said they are still adding speakers. About 100 Republican lawmakers and candidates are expected to attend the convention, which party strategists view as an effort to mobilize Trump voters ahead of November.
